flags.summary: The sales manager teaches reps to justify the deposit to prospects by saying the company does no follow-ups and does not re-book people, while the same meeting has reps planning follow-up calls and the manager scripting a follow-up message.
evidence: We do a deposit with people because we don't do any follow-ups. We don't put people back on the calendar because we get so busy with people.
And this is the process we put in place because we've had people who said they're going to come back and they don't.
Hit some follow-up. Yeah, I'm definitely going to.
How would you follow up with him? I would reach out and say, hey, I know things ended abruptly there.

flags.summary: A live deal is described at a $1,200 total paid in instalments, against the stated offer of $6,000/6mo or $9,000/12mo, for a prospect previously described as having minus $67 in his bank account.
evidence: Do you remember that guy had minus 67 bucks on his bank account?
He did actually pay a deposit.
he gets paid bi-weekly. And he said, like... Yeah, he said, like, I get paid at that time, but I can do the full $1,200 at that time.

flags.summary: Refundable deposits of $100 or $500 are coached as a standard step, a price point outside the two stated offer tiers.
evidence: Because there's really no risk. It's $500 or it's $100. There's no risk. They can get it right back.
This is the process. It's a $100 deposit. We send it right back to you.

flags.summary: A closer asked the manager to let him log a lost deal as a financial DQ specifically so his close rate would not be affected; the manager instructed him to log it accurately instead.
evidence: I was asking if you're okay with me putting it as an FDQ to make sure that my closing rate doesn't get destroyed
So don't worry about that so much. Put it in accurately how it's supposed to be put in.

flags.summary: A closer recommends calling non-responsive prospects from a number they will not recognise in order to get them to pick up and close them, and the manager does not correct it.
evidence: And if he doesn't respond, just give him a call on a random number on Monday.
if you call someone on the number that they know you from, they're not responding. But if you don't call them with a random number, they pick up.
And then you just ask a question. You can actually still close them because you just catch them.

flags.summary: A closer repeatedly refers to prospects by their sexual orientation and the team jokes about offering a prospect a date as a closing bonus; the manager pushes back only at the end.
evidence: Hat-trick. Well, where is it? gay guys in a row.
Chris, quick question. Should I send any message to Mr. Gay Guy?
Just call and be like, hey, baby, do you want to go out with me if you buy the program? I'll come as a bonus.
Tom is just a guy. It doesn't matter who he's attracted to or how is whatever. None of that matters.

flags.summary: An automated messaging system contacts leads without disclosure and has been spamming them with reminders after they reschedule; at least one prospect identified the messages as automated and complained, and another refused to attend.
evidence: he didn't like the fact that SalesKake kept sending things, even though they didn't get an answer on their question
he's like, hey, you can reschedule right here, but then it still pushes, your meeting starts in 15 minutes
a guy pointed it out, like, I don't know who's that, but that's probably automated. It's so annoying.
we were trying to do that AI bot thing, and it was decent... That was the name of the bot.
